turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“I’ve been feeling very confused lately, and I can’t really explain things the way I usually can. I’ve also had a fever and discomfort in my right upper abdomen.”

When did the confusion and trouble expressing yourself start, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?
When did the confusion and trouble expressing yourself start, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?
“It started a short time ago, and it felt like it came on fairly suddenly. I’ve been more confused since then, and I can’t seem to get my thoughts out clearly.”
Have you noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, dark urine, or pale stools?
“I haven’t noticed my eyes or skin looking yellow, and I don’t think my urine has turned dark, but I’m not fully sure because I’ve been so confused. I’m also not sure about my stool color.”
Are you having nausea or vomiting, and is the right upper abdominal discomfort constant or does it come and go, especially after eating?

“I haven’t been able to tell clearly about nausea or vomiting, but I don’t think I’ve been throwing up. The discomfort in my right upper abdomen feels more constant than just coming and going, and I haven’t noticed a clear pattern after eating.”
Have you had shaking chills or rigors, or has anyone measured how high your fever has been?

“I’ve had a fever and I feel quite unwell, but I’m not sure about shaking chills or rigors. I don’t remember anyone measuring how high it got because I’ve been very confused, though I do believe the fever was noticed.”
Any weakness or numbness on one side, facial droop, severe headache, vision changes, or trouble understanding speech in addition to trouble expressing yourself?

“I don’t think I’ve noticed one-sided weakness, numbness, or facial drooping, and I haven’t had a severe headache. I’m not sure about vision changes or trouble understanding speech because my confusion makes it hard to tell.”
Have you had any recent alcohol use, liver disease, gallstones, prior biliary procedures, or new medications?

“I don’t drink alcohol, and I don’t know of any liver disease or gallstones. I haven’t had any procedures in that area, and I can’t confidently say about new medications because I haven’t been able to keep track well.”
Any pain or burning with urination, cough, shortness of breath, or recent infections elsewhere?

“I don’t think I’ve had any pain or burning when I urinate, and I haven’t noticed a cough or trouble breathing. I’m not aware of any infection anywhere else, but I can’t say for sure because I’m so confused.”

[DDX] Acute cholangitis, acute cholecystitis with sepsis-associated encephalopathy, hepatic encephalopathy from acute hepatobiliary disease, pyogenic liver abscess, acute ischemic stroke/aphasia

This combination of fever, constant right upper quadrant discomfort, and acute confusion strongly raises concern for a serious hepatobiliary infection, especially acute cholangitis even without obvious jaundice. Acute cholecystitis with systemic infection is also very plausible. The language difficulty could be encephalopathy from sepsis, but stroke remains an important alternative because of the sudden trouble expressing thoughts.

This needs emergency in-person evaluation now if not already in the ED:
- vitals and sepsis assessment
- neurologic exam and stroke evaluation
- CBC, CMP, liver tests, bilirubin, INR, lactate, blood cultures
- RUQ ultrasound, possibly CT/MRCP depending on findings
- brain imaging if aphasia/confusion is focal or sudden
- urgent antibiotics if infection suspected

If you want, I can also explain why cholangitis is highest on the list and what findings would distinguish it from stroke or cholecystitis.
